title: Toolbar
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.TopAppBar (its actions slot with MonarchIconButton and MonarchMenu) and androidx.compose.material3.BottomAppBar, with MonarchChip in a horizontally scrolling Row for filters
summary: The controls above a list (search, view switch, export, filters) live in the Material 3 top app bar's actions and the bottom app bar, not in a row drawn by Monarch.
whenToUse: For the actions of a screen or a list: put one to three icon actions in TopAppBar(actions = …), move the rest to an overflow MonarchMenu, put thumb-reach actions in a BottomAppBar, and filters in a row of MonarchChips under the bar.
whenNotToUse: Not for the formatting controls of an editor or a field: use a SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow or icon toggle buttons next to the field. Not for Save and Discard on a form: use MonarchFormActionsBar.
api: @Composable fun TopAppBar(title: @Composable () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, navigationIcon: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit = {}, expandedHeight: Dp = TopAppBarDefaults.TopAppBarExpandedHeight, windowInsets: WindowInsets = TopAppBarDefaults.windowInsets, colors: TopAppBarColors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(), scrollBehavior: TopAppBarScrollBehavior? = null)

@Composable fun BottomAppBar(actions: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, floatingActionButton: @Composable (() -> Unit)? = null, containerColor: Color = BottomAppBarDefaults.containerColor, …)

@Composable fun MonarchIconButton(label: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = MonarchButtonSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, loadingLabel: String? = null, shape: Shape? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, icon: @Composable () -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchChip(text: String, selected: Boolean, onSelectedChange: (Boolean) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, size: MonarchTagSize = MonarchTagSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, selectedIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

states.name: actions
states.description: Icon actions sit at the end of the top app bar; each is a MonarchIconButton with a 48dp target.

states.name: overflow
states.description: Further actions are MonarchMenuItems in a menu opened from a More MonarchIconButton.

states.name: filters
states.description: MonarchChips under the bar show the selected filter with a fill and a check mark slot.

states.name: scrolled
states.description: With a TopAppBarScrollBehavior the bar changes to the scrolled container color or collapses (system behavior).

states.name: disabled
states.description: An MonarchIconButton or MonarchChip with enabled = false uses the disabled colors and is announced as disabled.

appearance: The app bars use the colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the canvas or raised background role for the container and the default text role for the title and icons. Filter chips use the outline border, and the accent subtle fill when selected. High-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web Toolbar is a role="toolbar" row with search at the start, grouped controls, trailing controls, a filters row and roving arrow-key focus. On Android the app bars are the toolbar: the system places the actions, the app moves extra actions into an overflow menu, and a hardware keyboard moves between them with Tab. Search is a MonarchSearchBar or the Material 3 SearchBar under or in place of the bar. Monarch ships no toolbar type. iOS uses its navigation bar and bottom bar in the same way.
accessibility: Each icon action is a MonarchIconButton with a content description ("Search", "More actions"), read as a button (system behavior).
MonarchIconButtons and MonarchChips have 48dp touch targets (system behavior).
A MonarchChip is read with its label and its selected state.
The title of a TopAppBar is plain text; mark it as a heading with Modifier.semantics { heading() } when the screen has no other heading.
edgeCases: Too many actions crowd the bar on a 320dp phone; keep one to three and move the rest to the overflow menu.
A filter row with many chips scrolls horizontally; it does not wrap.
Inside a Scaffold, pass the bar as topBar or bottomBar so the content is padded by its height.
